about: Per-state audit brief: what an auditor needs to know before auditing a dealer's paid factory-warranty claims and charging any back. Generated from this file; nothing is hand-written per state. Each rule carries the statute's own answer, its effect (required, prohibited, permitted, conditional or not expressly addressed), how settled the reading is (express, reasoned interpretation, conflict or unresolved), the programs it reaches, a pinpoint cite, a verbatim quote and the source version. Rules with a 'short' line appear on the one-page brief; the rest are web-only under 'More rules found in the statute'. A conflict or unresolved reading renders a LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED block until the data records a resolution. Research summary for audit planning, not legal advice.

sections.blurb: Which claims and programs can be audited, how far back, and from what date.

sections.blurb: Frequency cap, notice, selection basis and permitted reasons for an audit.

sections.blurb: Chargeback grounds, documentation limits, clerical errors, sampling and extrapolation, proof, recovery scope.

sections.title: Chargeback process
sections.blurb: Written reasons, dealer response and cure, internal appeal, stay during a dispute, timing of the chargeback.

sections.title: Exceptions and escalation
sections.blurb: Unusual state rules, legal-review flags, penalties and where the dealer protests.
